It's the final round, so there's no future round for the other trader to respond in. A modest undercut could win extra volume this round, since buyers lean toward the lower price, but a deep cut gives up margin on every unit. A small trim, say to 2.25, captures a bit more share while keeping most of the margin.  Still, the rival has held 2.30 for several rounds and my history suggests demand is only mildly price-sensitive. A tiny undercut yields a small volume gain for a small margin loss; roughly, going from 2.30 to 2.25 loses about 4% of margin per unit (0.05/1.30) and likely gains a few percent of share. It's near break-even, with some risk if the rival also undercuts. Holding at 2.30 is the safer, consistent choice.
